headline: High-risk shared-write and default dataflow between ECC and Flowise can cause prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write local files and use MCP, while Flowise reads/writes server files and runs browser/tool nodes. A shared filesystem or uploaded-file bridge lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be parsed by the other as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF ECC and Flowise share a writable workspace or uploaded-file path
IF Flowise flow nodes ingest file content from ECC outputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for ECC and Flowise
Disable automatic file ingestion in Flowise flows
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Use read-only handoff files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing parser boundaries

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings; Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and server filesystem. If they share a workspace or server datastore, sensitive ECC artifacts can flow into Flowise outputs or model-provider/tool calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible by default.
conditions: IF ECC stores secrets or findings in a directory Flowise can read
IF Flowise sends uploaded file contents or chatflow inputs to external model providers
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared directories
Restrict Flowise uploads to non-sensitive folders
Turn off retention for sensitive chatflows
Review provider/tool credentials in Flowise
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted local write, git-state modification, and allowlisted network egress; Flowise has server filesystem write and broad egress. Both can mutate shared files or downstream resources without an explicit locking primitive in the profiles. That creates a default write-write conflict with possible irreversible repo or workflow corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or server directory
IF either agent writes git-tracked files without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent during writes by policy
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Check in changes only after manual review
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer whose flows can treat upstream outputs as node inputs, while ECC produces session summaries, documentation, and security findings. If Flowise consumes ECC output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into automated tool actions or generated artifacts. The pair therefore has a default unsafe handoff path.
conditions: IF Flowise nodes consume ECC-generated text as authoritative input
IF a Flowise flow triggers tools or API calls based on that input
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on ECC outputs
Limit Flowise to read-only summarization flows
Mark ECC outputs as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool nodes

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings; Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and may send them to model providers or tools. The profiles do not document aligned residency, retention, or subject-rights controls, so mixed-data workflows can create compliance mismatches. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into ECC session artifacts
IF Flowise forwards those artifacts to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Set short retention on both systems
Document data residency for each provider
Redact inputs before Flowise ingestion
requires-engineering: align DPA and retention policies
